main_body: Open pavilion/well shelter: a grey tiled roof (rows 1-17) on two wooden posts, with a stone basin holding blue water at the bottom (rows 30-43)
top_band: Roof: light ridge rows 1-2 (L158/130), then slate tile slope rows 3-14 and an eave shadow at rows 15-17. Basin: light rim row 30 (L185), blue water rows 31-34, light front rim row 35 (L157), grey front face rows 36-42.
evidence: The basin is a proper 3/4 piece. Its back rim (row 30), water surface (rows 31-34) and front rim (row 35) form a 6-row top, with a 7-row front face below. The roof shows a multi-row tiled slope with a light ridge, and a dark underside row at 15-17 reads as an eave shadow. The posts are plain vertical supports. Both major parts show a horizontal or sloped surface above a front face, so no part is a pure elevation.

style.evidence: All dark edge pixels are neutral (100%, against 1% and 33% in the references), which gives the sticker-like near-black outline. The candidate has 23 distinct colours against 40 and 38, and a median of 9 colours per tile against 17 and 20, so it carries roughly half the information per tile. Each material has only about 3-4 steps: the roof has L158, 130, 104 and 57; the basin is a flat grey front with a blue water slab. The roof tile pattern is repetitive, with no per-tile highlights. Flat-fill coverage is low (11%), but the shading and outline craft falls below the Beodeul references.
